content.value_statement: Agents lose context across sessions and can act on stale facts. This skill helps design persistent memory with retrieval, graphs, temporal validity, and benchmarks.
actual_capabilities: Compares Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta, Cognee, LangMem, and file-system memory by retrieval fit.
Explains memory layers from working context to temporal knowledge graphs.
Maps query shapes to semantic, entity, temporal, and hybrid retrieval.
Provides Python examples for vector stores, property graphs, temporal relationships, and integrated memory retrieval.
Lists consolidation triggers and recovery strategies for stale, conflicting, or empty retrievals.
References benchmarks and papers for memory system evaluation.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a hosted memory service.
Benchmark references can become outdated and should be rechecked before product claims.
Sample implementations use simplified embedding and graph logic.
It does not replace privacy, retention, or deletion policy design.

use_cases.title: Plan Agent Memory Architecture
use_cases.description: Choose the simplest persistent memory layer for an agent before adding graph or temporal storage.

use_cases.title: Compare Memory Frameworks
use_cases.description: Evaluate Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta, Cognee, LangMem, and file-system options against retrieval needs.

use_cases.title: Design Memory Evaluation
use_cases.description: Select benchmarks and failure checks for long conversation recall, stale facts, and multi-hop retrieval.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starting Layer
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the simplest memory layer for an agent that [task]. Include storage choice, retrieval method, and when to upgrade.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Frameworks
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta, Cognee, LangMem, and file-system memory for [project]. Rank them by fit and risk.

prompt_templates.title: Design Temporal Memory
prompt_templates.scenario: Handling facts that change over time.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a temporal memory model for facts that change over time in [domain]. Include entity identity, validity periods, conflict handling, and retrieval flow.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this memory architecture: [details]. Identify retrieval failure modes, privacy controls, consolidation triggers, benchmark plan, and migration steps.

output_examples.input: Design memory for a support agent that remembers customer preferences.
output: Start with session-scoped facts plus entity records for each customer.
Add semantic retrieval when agents need similarity search across many interactions.
Add temporal validity for preferences that can change, such as plan, address, or contact channel.

output_examples.input: Compare Graphiti and file-system memory for a research assistant.
output_examples.output: File-system memory is better for a small prototype with simple notes. Graphiti is stronger when the assistant needs temporal facts, entity relationships, and multi-hop queries.

output_examples.input: Find risks in a memory design that loads all stored facts into every prompt.
output: The design wastes context budget and can reduce answer quality.
It increases privacy exposure because unrelated memories enter the active prompt.
Use just-in-time retrieval with entity, time, and relevance filters instead.

best_practices: Start with the simplest durable memory layer that meets the retrieval need.
Track validity periods for facts that can change over time.
Benchmark retrieval quality before and after adding graph or hybrid search.
anti_patterns: Loading every stored memory into the active prompt.
Treating stale facts as current without validity checks.
Adding a complex graph schema before proving simpler retrieval fails.

faq.question: Is this a memory database?
faq.answer: No. It is a design and implementation guide for choosing or building memory systems.

faq.question: Can it help choose between Mem0 and Graphiti?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares frameworks by retrieval shape, temporal needs, multi-hop reasoning, and production trade-offs.

faq.question: Does it store user data by itself?
faq.answer: No. The skill includes examples only. Any real storage depends on the system you build.

faq.question: What tools support this skill?
faq.answer: It is declared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use temporal memory?
faq.answer: Use it when facts change over time and queries need the state for a specific date.

faq.question: What should I check before production?
faq.answer: Check privacy controls, retention rules, deletion workflows, benchmark results, latency, and memory growth.
